text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing intermittent NCCL multi-node failures in rack-17/zone-a. All-reduce aborts with 'peer has disconnected' on 2-3 nodes per day. Anyone else?

ajay: Yep, spotted at ~0300 UTC. Started after the node NIC/fw rolling last week. Jobs hit 'Unreachable error' inside NCCL.

infra-bot: Alert: mlx5 tx_restart increment on host gpu-node-17-3 (counter tx_restart=1) — https://infra.logs/1768123456/metrics :eyes: 

leo: Can you paste dmesg and mlx5 stats from a failed host?

maria: Paste from gpu-node-17-3 around crash:
```
[12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: mlx5e: tx_restart occured on port 1
[12345.678905] ib_core: QP 0x1f to ERR state
[12345.678910] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: HW: completion with error on SQ 2
```

ajay: ethtool -S shows increasing tx_packets_dropped and tx_restart_count. ran: `ethtool -S mlx5_core | egrep -i "tx|restart|drop"` output looked noisy.

kai: Quick hypothesis: RoCEv2 + ECN + large MTU causing sporadic drops under incast. Did we change MTU on the TOR or upgrade switch firmware recently? Also check for offload regressions (TSO/GSO/SW checks).

leo: I ran ib_write_bw style probe and saw occasional WR flush / CQ errors. `ibv_devinfo` shows firmware 16.27.1013 on affected hosts.

sre-oncall: We rolled NIC firmware from 16.27.1000 -> 16.27.1013 last Tue as part of stability fixes. Opening vendor ticket in parallel. Short-term mitigation ideas?

ajay: For one test node I disabled TSO and GSO and the NCCL job ran stable for ~6h with same workload. Not a proof but promising: `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off`

maria: Repro plan: run NCCL allreduce across 8 nodes in rack-17 with load-generator + iperf to simulate incast. Want to try toggling kernel params too: net.core.netdev_max_backlog, txqueuelen.

kai: I'll also try reproducing in lab with same firmware + same TOR switch model. Plan to enable mlx5 debug flags and collect stack traces if we hit tx_restart.

leo: Additional data: `ethtool -S` on gpu-node-17-3 snippet:
```
mlx5_0_tx_restart_count: 3
mlx5_0_tx_pause_pkts: 0
mlx5_0_tx_dropped: 124
```

ajay: Captured packet-level evidence with tcpdump on eth0 for RoCE UDP port (4791). Saw retransmits and malformed UDP segments aligned with NCCL failures. Command used: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 4791 -w roce-dump.pcap`

infra-bot: Created INFRA ticket INFRA-4872 and attached initial logs + pcap: https://tickets/INFRA-4872 (vendor engaged) :ticket: 

sre-oncall: Short-term policy: restrict cross-rack NCCL all-reduce scheduling from rack-17 for 24h and prefer nodes with older NIC fw as a safety zone. Also throttle large parallel cross-rack runs.

maria: ACK. I'll add a placement constraint in the scheduler (rack affinity) and post a status in #incidents if this escalates.

kai: If we can repro in lab I'll try kernel-side: `modprobe mlx5_core debug=0x1` and enable stack traces on tx_restart. Also test disabling SRQ and toggle flow control (pause frames).

leo: Note: 3 other hosts on the same TOR model show tx_restart bumps with same fw. Tor vendor config might interact with new NIC firmware — checking pause frame and priority flow control (PFC) settings.

ajay: Observed that two nodes still on older fw (16.27.1000) haven't shown the issue under heavy load. Points to firmware regression + switch offload interplay.

maria: Good. Priorities: 1) schedule lab repro, 2) vendor ticket + logs (INFRA-4872), 3) scheduler placement rollback or affinity rule. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

kai: I'll take kernel debug tonight if lab repro confirmed. Ping me when you have repro script.

sre-oncall: I'll coordinate the placement patch and keep the ticket updated.

maria: will post short update in #incidents and ping infra on-call.

---
Notes: we should capture `dmesg`, `ethtool -S`, `ibv_devinfo`, `rdma stats`, `tcpdump (udp 4791)`, and NCCL logs (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) for vendor. Workaround validated: disable TSO/GSO reduces failures in short runs.
